audit_status.source_base: Greek Hebrews text tradition, with Septuagint Psalm 8 and other citation texture; draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for warning, humanity crowned, Jesus made lower than messengers, shared flesh/blood, death defeated, merciful faithful high priest.

verses.restored: Because of this it is necessary for us to pay more abundant attention to what was heard, lest we drift away.

familiar.text: Therefore we ought to give the more earnest heed to the things which we have heard, lest at any time we should let them slip.

modern.text: We must pay closer attention, therefore, to what we have heard, so that we do not drift away.

original.text: Διὰ τοῦτο δεῖ περισσοτέρως ⸂προσέχειν ἡμᾶς⸃ τοῖς ἀκουσθεῖσιν, μήποτε παραρυῶμεν.

verses.restored: For if the word spoken through messengers became firm, and every transgression and disobedience received just repayment,

familiar.text: For if the word spoken by angels was stedfast, and every transgression and disobedience received a just recompence of reward;

modern.text: For if the message spoken by angels was binding, and every transgression and disobedience received its just punishment,

original.text: εἰ γὰρ ὁ διʼ ἀγγέλων λαληθεὶς λόγος ἐγένετο βέβαιος, καὶ πᾶσα παράβασις καὶ παρακοὴ ἔλαβεν ἔνδικον μισθαποδοσίαν,

verses.restored: how will we escape if we neglect so great salvation/healing, which took beginning of being spoken through the Lord and was confirmed to us by those who heard,

familiar.text: How shall we escape, if we neglect so great salvation; which at the first began to be spoken by the Lord, and was confirmed unto us by them that heard him;

modern.text: how shall we escape if we neglect such a great salvation? This salvation was first announced by the Lord, was confirmed to us by those who heard Him,

original.text: πῶς ἡμεῖς ἐκφευξόμεθα τηλικαύτης ἀμελήσαντες σωτηρίας, ἥτις, ἀρχὴν λαβοῦσα λαλεῖσθαι διὰ τοῦ κυρίου, ὑπὸ τῶν ἀκουσάντων εἰς ἡμᾶς ἐβεβαιώθη,

verses.restored: the Divine bearing witness together by signs, wonders, various powers, and distributions of holy Spirit according to his will?

familiar.text: God also bearing them witness, both with signs and wonders, and with divers miracles, and gifts of the Holy Ghost, according to his own will?

modern.text: and was affirmed by God through signs, wonders, various miracles, and gifts of the Holy Spirit distributed according to His will. Jesus like His Brothers

original.text: συνεπιμαρτυροῦντος τοῦ θεοῦ σημείοις τε καὶ τέρασιν καὶ ποικίλαις δυνάμεσιν καὶ πνεύματος ἁγίου μερισμοῖς κατὰ τὴν αὐτοῦ θέλησιν;

verses.restored: For not to messengers did he arrange the inhabited world to come, concerning which we speak.

familiar.text: For unto the angels hath he not put in subjection the world to come, whereof we speak.

modern.text: For it is not to angels that He has subjected the world to come, about which we are speaking.

original.text: Οὐ γὰρ ἀγγέλοις ὑπέταξεν τὴν οἰκουμένην τὴν μέλλουσαν, περὶ ἧς λαλοῦμεν·

verses.restored: But someone testified somewhere, saying: What is human that you remember him, or son of human that you visit him?

familiar.text: But one in a certain place testified, saying, What is man, that thou art mindful of him? or the son of man, that thou visitest him?

modern.text: But somewhere it is testified in these words: “What is man that You are mindful of him, or the son of man that You care for him?

original.text: διεμαρτύρατο δέ πού τις λέγων· Τί ἐστιν ἄνθρωπος ὅτι μιμνῄσκῃ αὐτοῦ, ἢ υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου ὅτι ἐπισκέπτῃ αὐτόν;

verses.restored: You made him a little lower than messengers; with glory and honor you crowned him.

familiar.text: Thou madest him a little lower than the angels; thou crownedst him with glory and honour, and didst set him over the works of thy hands:

modern.text: You made him a little lower than the angels; You crowned him with glory and honor

original.text: ἠλάττωσας αὐτὸν βραχύ τι παρʼ ἀγγέλους, δόξῃ καὶ τιμῇ ἐστεφάνωσας ⸀αὐτόν,

verses.restored: You arranged all things under his feet. For in arranging all things under him, he left nothing unarranged. Yet now we do not yet see all things arranged under him.

familiar.text: Thou hast put all things in subjection under his feet. For in that he put all in subjection under him, he left nothing that is not put under him. But now we see not yet all things put under him.

modern.text: and placed everything under his feet.” When God subjected all things to him, He left nothing outside of his control. Yet at present we do not see everything subject to him.

original.text: πάντα ὑπέταξας ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν αὐτοῦ· ἐν ⸂τῷ γὰρ⸃ ⸀ὑποτάξαι τὰ πάντα οὐδὲν ἀφῆκεν αὐτῷ ἀνυπότακτον. νῦν δὲ οὔπω ὁρῶμεν αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα ὑποτεταγμένα·

verses.restored: But we see Jesus, made a little lower than messengers because of suffering of death, crowned with glory and honor, so that by grace of Divine he might taste death on behalf of everyone.

familiar.text: But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour; that he by the grace of God should taste death for every man.

modern.text: But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels, now crowned with glory and honor because He suffered death, so that by the grace of God He might taste death for everyone.

original.text: τὸν δὲ βραχύ τι παρʼ ἀγγέλους ἠλαττωμένον βλέπομεν Ἰησοῦν διὰ τὸ πάθημα τοῦ θανάτου δόξῃ καὶ τιμῇ ἐστεφανωμένον, ὅπως ⸀χωρὶς θεοῦ ὑπὲρ παντὸς γεύσηται θανάτου.

verses.restored: For it was fitting for him, because of whom are all things and through whom are all things, bringing many children into glory, to complete the pioneer/founder of their salvation/healing through sufferings.

familiar.text: For it became him, for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings.

modern.text: In bringing many sons to glory, it was fitting for God, for whom and through whom all things exist, to make the author of their salvation perfect through suffering.

original.text: Ἔπρεπεν γὰρ αὐτῷ, διʼ ὃν τὰ πάντα καὶ διʼ οὗ τὰ πάντα, πολλοὺς υἱοὺς εἰς δόξαν ἀγαγόντα τὸν ἀρχηγὸν τῆς σωτηρίας αὐτῶν διὰ παθημάτων τελειῶσαι.

verses.restored: For the one sanctifying and those being sanctified are all from one; because of this he is not ashamed to call them siblings,

familiar.text: For both he that sanctifieth and they who are sanctified are all of one: for which cause he is not ashamed to call them brethren,

modern.text: For both the One who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are of the same family. So Jesus is not ashamed to call them brothers.

original.text: ὅ τε γὰρ ἁγιάζων καὶ οἱ ἁγιαζόμενοι ἐξ ἑνὸς πάντες· διʼ ἣν αἰτίαν οὐκ ἐπαισχύνεται ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοὺς καλεῖν,

verses.restored: saying: I will announce your name to my siblings; in midst of assembly I will hymn you.

familiar.text: Saying, I will declare thy name unto my brethren, in the midst of the church will I sing praise unto thee.

modern.text: He says: “I will proclaim Your name to My brothers; I will sing Your praises in the assembly.”

original.text: λέγων· Ἀπαγγελῶ τὸ ὄνομά σου τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς μου, ἐν μέσῳ ἐκκλησίας ὑμνήσω σε·

verses.restored: And again: I will trust in him. And again: Look, I and the children whom the Divine gave me.

familiar.text: And again, I will put my trust in him. And again, Behold I and the children which God hath given me.

modern.text: And again: “I will put My trust in Him.” And once again: “Here am I, and the children God has given Me.”

original.text: καὶ πάλιν· Ἐγὼ ἔσομαι πεποιθὼς ἐπʼ αὐτῷ· καὶ πάλιν· Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ καὶ τὰ παιδία ἅ μοι ἔδωκεν ὁ θεός.

verses.restored: Therefore, since the children have shared in blood and flesh, he himself likewise shared the same things, so that through death he might make inactive the one having power of death, that is, the slanderer/adversary,

familiar.text: Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same; that through death he might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil;

modern.text: Now since the children have flesh and blood, He too shared in their humanity, so that by His death He might destroy him who holds the power of death, that is, the devil,

original.text: Ἐπεὶ οὖν τὰ παιδία κεκοινώνηκεν ⸂αἵματος καὶ σαρκός⸃, καὶ αὐτὸς παραπλησίως μετέσχεν τῶν αὐτῶν, ἵνα διὰ τοῦ θανάτου καταργήσῃ τὸν τὸ κράτος ἔχοντα τοῦ θανάτου, τοῦτʼ ἔστι τὸν διάβολον,

verses.restored: and release these, as many as through fear of death were held in slavery through all their life.

familiar.text: And deliver them who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage.

modern.text: and free those who all their lives were held in slavery by their fear of death.

original.text: καὶ ἀπαλλάξῃ τούτους, ὅσοι φόβῳ θανάτου διὰ παντὸς τοῦ ζῆν ἔνοχοι ἦσαν δουλείας.

verses.restored: For surely he does not take hold of messengers, but he takes hold of seed of Abraham.

familiar.text: For verily he took not on him the nature of angels; but he took on him the seed of Abraham.

modern.text: For surely it is not the angels He helps, but the descendants of Abraham.

original.text: οὐ γὰρ δήπου ἀγγέλων ἐπιλαμβάνεται, ἀλλὰ σπέρματος Ἀβραὰμ ἐπιλαμβάνεται.

verses.restored: Therefore he owed in all things to be made like the siblings, so that he might become merciful and trustworthy high priest in things toward the Divine, to make atoning mercy for the sins/misalignments of the people.

familiar.text: Wherefore in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren, that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest in things pertaining to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people.

modern.text: For this reason He had to be made like His brothers in every way, so that He might become a merciful and faithful high priest in service to God, in order to make atonement for the sins of the people.

original.text: ὅθεν ὤφειλεν κατὰ πάντα τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς ὁμοιωθῆναι, ἵνα ἐλεήμων γένηται καὶ πιστὸς ἀρχιερεὺς τὰ πρὸς τὸν θεόν, εἰς τὸ ἱλάσκεσθαι τὰς ἁμαρτίας τοῦ λαοῦ·

verses.restored: For in what he himself has suffered, being tested, he is able to help those being tested.

familiar.text: For in that he himself hath suffered being tempted, he is able to succour them that are tempted.

modern.text: Because He Himself suffered when He was tempted, He is able to help those who are being tempted.

original.text: ἐν ᾧ γὰρ πέπονθεν αὐτὸς πειρασθείς, δύναται τοῖς πειραζομένοις βοηθῆσαι.

translation_notes: Psalm 8 is read christologically but also preserves human vocation: all things not yet seen subject.
Jesus shares blood and flesh; incarnation is solidarity, not escape from embodiment.
High priest language begins as mercy, trustworthiness, and help for tested people.
safety_note: Hebrews 2 uses warning language, but its pastoral center is release from fear of death and merciful help for tested humans.
